To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the alkylation of 5-tertiary-substituted tetra-zoles by tertiary alcohols in sulfuric acid proceeds selectively at the 2-position, whereas the alkylation by tertiary alcohol in phosphoric acid is selective at the 1-position.

the alkylation of a tetrazole ring by alcohols is a regioselective process that results in the formation, in the case of tetrazole itself, of 2-alkylderivatives, and that in the case of 5-substitued tetrazoles the 2-alkylation prevails irrespective of the nature of the 5-substituent.

alkylation of 5-tertiary-substituted tetra-zoles by alcohals in sulfuric acid leads to the formation of 2-substitut-ed tetrazoles, and that alkylation by alcohols of 5-methyltetrazole, 5-phenyltetrazole, and 5-(4-methylphenyl) tetrazole in sulfuric acid also leads to the formation 2-substitued derivatives.

a novel and efficient approach to the synthesis of a variety of tetrazolylalkylamines, which can be used as intermediates for the preparation of biologically active compounds.
the selective synthesis of 2-alkyldiazenes from aliphatic amines.
the selective alkylation of the N(2)-position of tetrazole ring by various alcohols in strong acid media.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the alkylation of 5-substitued tetrazoles by 5-alkyl alcohols results in the formation only of the 2-alkylation products.

the alkylation of the tetrazoles with the alcohols in the presence of the acids proceeds with the formation of the 1-alkyltetazoles in the case of phosphoric acid and the 2-alkyldiazoles when sulfuric acid is used.
alcohols alkylate tetrazole and tetrazoles at nitrogen-2 and not at nitrogen-1.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the alkylation of 5-substituent derivatives of tetrazole is a selective process and that the 2-alkylation of the tetrazoles is the only reaction that occurs in concentrated sulfuric acid.
the alkylation of 5-substituent tetrazoles by primary and secondary alcohols is a selective reaction that results in the formation, in high yields, of 2-alkoxytetrazoles.
the alkylation of the tetrazoles with alcohols in sulfuric acid is a selective process, and the 2-alkylation predominates.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the N(2) position of tetrazole is more reactive than the 1-position, which is in contrast to what was reported in a previous study.
the 2-alkylation of tetrazoles is a highly selective process, which is not affected by the nature of the substituent in the tetrazole molecule.
5-substituents of tetrazoles can be used as protecting groups, which are easily removed by alkylation with an alcohol.
